approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It draws breeding parents from score quantiles, makes fresh candidates by connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond edits, checks molecular identity and source-relative sulfur changes, and retains high-scoring survivors. Before each purchase batch it fits a Gaussian process to the current session's accepted scores using count-Morgan fingerprints and generalized Tanimoto covariance. Ten correlated function draws select distinct members of a fresh pool; after three non-improving batches, eligibility is restricted to the forty highest original GP means. The Parent has already removed an unexposed rejection-conditioned mutation-call floor, while retaining ordinary sampled mutation continuation. Its learned score location, correlated residual, and real accepted-feedback loop are active capabilities.
approach.novelty: Add one cardinal molecular-pair regressor at the predictive-location consumer. It learns signed raw-score differences from every ordered pair of accepted molecules and predicts each candidate relative to the earliest accepted incumbent. These locations replace the original GP locations only in sampled purchase values; the original GP still determines residuals and eligibility. Unlike the ordinal-preference sibling, the training target retains score magnitude. Unlike the earlier bootstrap-tree replacement, it leaves the GP residual law intact. This tests whether a magnitude-aware conditional predictor improves prospective errors and changes useful purchases, without assuming that better prediction will improve final scores.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting observed behavior is weak conversion of continuing purchases into new incumbent gains, especially late, while a useful but imperfect original GP location is retained. Direct audits of the actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de's fifteen Search logs and trajectories find 435 full pools, 4350 paid optimizer purchases, 88 restricted pools and no posterior fallback; only 253 purchases improve the incumbent and 76 do so in optimizer ordinals 146..290. Full/late incumbent-increment mass is 5.978073077532332 / 1.0224077547621127. Its complete original summaries give mean 0.607030316211131, population seed SD 0.030175277546149237 and seed macros 0.649701282562401 / 0.585233817344553 / 0.586155848726439. On its actual paid stream the original GP MSE is 0.01159945132539192 and strict within-batch ordering accuracy is 0.7064888432931521; these are descriptive selected-stream quantities, not proof that the predictor caused the late deficit. The Parent has no learned cardinal molecular-pair predictor. The frozen source evidence supplies a specific testable alternative: sparse ordinal n-aaeb1a1ac082 lost 0.101371920532155 versus this Parent and its likelihood omitted score magnitudes; complete ordinal n-b37d60f71872 improved its registered pooled ordering but still reached only 0.47969672018590265, with passive raw GP ordering better. Its confirmed ordering verdict remains intact. The bootstrap CART n-7922cfd1903a improved selected-stream MSE 0.012718 to 0.010939 on different adaptive streams yet lost 0.0609765636321587 against its own Parent, so error benefit alone is not endpoint evidence. R70 n-645c611d69c8 raised modeled batch utility while preserving its mean and lost 0.0004071597452423396 against its own Parent; n-85ae5a42a8bb improved same-paid distributional loss with fixed raw GP location yet lost 0.029352868348309302. Their complete means are 0.5723948931348757 and 0.548162923889155. These are contrary results on their named hosts, not repetitions of the present location-only hypothesis. Exact source paths/hashes, all Parent cell audits, signed source endpoints and the distinction from the older aggregate narrative are preserved in policy/scratch/r0071-00-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files; underlying sources are nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-{0,1,2}/summary.json, run.log and the five individual logs/*.log and trajectories/*.jsonl files listed there, plus the six cited nodes' original analysis.json, policy node records and Search summaries.

method_change.previous_method: Original accepted-only count-Tanimoto GP location inside correlated sampled offspring allocation on n-cf8d309c06de.
method_change.proposed_method: Task-local all-ordered-pair raw-score XGBoost difference regressor, incumbent-referenced as active location, retaining original GP residual and original-mean eligibility.
method_change.rationale: The actual code Parent lacks cardinal molecular-pair regression. Its late progress is limited, and the frozen ordinal and R70 results support testing an explicitly magnitude-aware location capability while showing that predictive diagnostics alone do not guarantee an endpoint gain. This coordinated fit/reference/location integration is one component intervention on n-cf8d309c06de, not a whole-method replacement.

hypothesis: Modify only the active predictive location in the original correlated sampled allocator on code Parent n-cf8d309c06de. At each inherited pre-suggestion refit, sort the real accepted archive by its unchanged serial and form exactly n*n rows indexed k=i*n+j. Row k is concat(c_i,c_j), where c is the unchanged radius-2 chiral 2048-bin count-Morgan vector; its target is y_j-y_i in original score units. Both orientations and all n diagonal zeros remain, including zero off-diagonal differences and distinct accepted identities with aliased features. All rows carry equal default unit weight; n*n dependent pairs still contain only n accepted labels and supply no new independent observations. Fit a fresh fixed XGBoost 2.1.4 histogram squared-error regressor with the explicit registered parameters. Let b be the earliest-serial record attaining the largest accepted raw score at suggestion entry. Freeze this one reference for all ten unobserved choices. For every pool candidate x compute d(x)=D(concat(c_b,c_x)) and mu_delta(x)=y_b+d(x). Retain the original accepted-only GP fit, mean mu_GP, covariance, Cholesky/jitter and raw residual R=score_scale*(Z@L.T). Execute the original ten-row normal draw once and its original GP sample finite check. Active values are mu_delta[None,:]+R in float64, while the passive original values are mu_GP[None,:]+R. Eligibility remains exactly the original GP-mean K=3/M=40 rule; sequential availability, earliest-pool-index exact ties, graph laws, survival and feedback remain unchanged. No correction for D(b,b), antisymmetrization, averaging of references, location blending, residual rescaling, within-batch fantasy update, score transformation or greedy acquisition is introduced. Prediction: complete correct execution with at least one actually paid identity absent from the same-state original-GP selected set gives strictly lower all-paid mean squared prediction error for y_paid-y_b than mu_GP-y_b. A changed purchased identity, not mere floating-point location displacement, supplies meaningful direct exposure. The equality MSE(d, y-y_b)=MSE(mu_delta,y) is explicit: this primary test is also a paired raw-location-error comparison. It does not itself claim an endpoint mediator.

finding_summary.headline: Cardinal learning changed every batch, but predicted paid score differences worse than the original GP.
finding_summary.insights: This is an exposed scientific counterexample to the exact cardinal-location prediction, with no technical nonexecution or missing paid evidence. The borrowed ordered-pair construction and earliest-best reference operated faithfully; the declared count-feature, fixed-regressor and batch-ten GP-residual adaptations make this a new hybrid, so the finding does not adjudicate the source paper's full algorithm or all cardinal learning. Expanding accepted labels into millions of dependent pairs did not fix predictive ranking. A different property/difference model, potentially one that represents zero self-difference and opposite signed directions explicitly, is the kind of method needed to address the measured ranking and reference defects; this run does not establish that such a replacement would improve endpoints. More apparent progress also did not mean better search: the Child recorded 276 incumbent advances versus 253 descriptively for the Parent, and greater late increment mass (1.594 versus 1.022), yet less total increment mass (4.745 versus 5.978). The molecular evidence shows a second limitation of the realized search: broad scaffold totals coexist with similar batches and narrow leading families, plus a concentrated large-molecule tail (837 purchases at least 50 heavy atoms versus 46 descriptively for the Parent). Fragment-excluded within-batch similarity remains higher, so this pattern is not explained by tiny-fragment artifacts. This is local concentration rather than universal scaffold collapse; some leading series retain substantial core diversity. Coherent size-preserving core or ring changes are a proposal capability that could address that limitation, but this experiment leaves its benefit and any chemical mediation of the score open. Reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry further limit chemical interpretation. The result settles the registered prediction on this complete purchased stream; it does not end the approach or establish a general contribution verdict.
finding_summary.results: All 435 scheduled fits and all 4,350 paid prediction/label joins completed correctly. Every batch changed its selected set: 2,425 purchases were absent from the same-state original-GP selection. The registered prediction nevertheless failed. Cardinal mean squared error was 0.0093267 versus 0.00524075 for the passive GP on those same purchases, about 78.0% higher, and worse in all 15 task/seed cells. Paid ordering accuracy was 63.49% versus 69.12%, with prediction ties counted as half correct. Error improved on the 373 purchases above the announcement incumbent and 85 exact ties, but worsened on the 3,892 below it; those favorable subsets cannot replace the full-stream test. All three Search replicas completed their full budgets. The final mean score was 0.524843, compared with the archived Parent's 0.607030; eleven of fifteen task/seed endpoints were lower. The frozen comparator certifies no matched seeds because the registered XGBoost addition changes the environment lock, although all stage-profile hashes match. These endpoint differences remain descriptive, and the separate matched +0.002 criterion is not certified as evaluated.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich analogues with scarce tiny fragments, a large-molecule tail, reactive substituents and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This assessment reads all 15 Child and 15 published Parent Search trajectories for seeds 0/1/2, with 300 accepted observations per session. Chemical statistics exclude the supplied initial observations and describe 4,350 optimizer purchases per node. These are accepted, scored structures, not the entire unevaluated proposal pool. Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant: digest ring-closure rates are 0.9977 to 1.0 and aromatic-presence rates are 0.7276 to 1.0. The molecules include indole carboxamides, extended heteroaryl/aryl-ether assemblies, aryl-substituted cyclic amines, medium-ring lactams and heavily bridged fluorinated imide-like frameworks. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry motifs coexist with N-halogen bonds, peroxides, carbodiimide/cumulated-bond motifs, strained-looking ring junctions and electrophilic substituents. Makeability is therefore questionable overall; valence-valid SMILES and a favorable supplied score do not establish stability, synthesis or biological utility. The Child median is 32 heavy atoms (range 2-120), versus 28 (range 1-96) in the published Parent. For <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 heavy atoms, the Child counts are 4, 4, 837 and 828; Parent counts are 91, 98, 46 and 44. The large tail is concentrated rather than universal: one covered task contributes 746 of the Child's >=50-atom molecules. Across all tasks there are 2,038 typed and 1,366 generic Murcko scaffolds, versus 1,668 and 952 for the Parent; these totals include the empty acyclic scaffold and are not independent chemotypes or a measure of usefulness. Radius-2 chirality-aware 2,048-count Morgan dot-product Tanimoto, averaged over unordered pairs only within each task/seed cell, is 0.642373 for Child and 0.597975 for Parent; excluding <=6-heavy-atom molecules gives 0.643513 and 0.624922. Within purchase batches the corresponding means are 0.742229 and 0.685225, or 0.743529 and 0.715720 after fragment exclusion. Values are rounded, pair-count weighted, and never compare molecules across independent sessions. Thus broad scaffold counts coexist with locally similar batches and concentrated leading families. All 4,350 Child structures have no formal charges, assigned tetrahedral stereocentres or specified double-bond stereochemistry; RDKit finds 6,946 unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,757 of them. Basic amines and multiply halogenated carbons are present, so neither is an absent chemical capability in this record. The frozen comparison says child_complete=true, paired_complete=false, matched_seeds=[], and profile_mismatched_seeds=[0,1,2]. All supplied Parent trajectory paths exist, but the frozen context provides no certified paired comparison. Parent contrasts here are descriptive chemistry only; no component attribution, activation verdict, causal score effect or node selection follows. Child evidence remains the actual .worktrees/slot-0/runs/staging/seed-N/trajectories files named in the frozen request; no future Child archive is asserted. Input paths/hashes, exact per-task/per-seed statistics, source-specific witnesses, methods and all batch similarities are recorded in policy/scratch/r0071-00-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and its 15 audit-seed-N-task.json files. The top-87 descriptions below use the highest supplied scores among 870 optimizer records per task with fixed seed/evaluation tie handling; correlated analogues are not independent evidence.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 accepted optimizer records, heavy atoms range from 3 to 51 with median 26; the median perceived ring count is 3. Counts at <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 heavy atoms are respectively 1, 1, 2 and 2. Typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 248/107, versus 187/70 in the published Parent. The leading seed-0 and seed-2 families are compact, mostly planar N-aryl indole carboxamides with methyl, methoxy and halo substituents. The seed-0 leader has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, including an N-hydroxy amide and an N-bromomethyl substituent. The seed-2 leader also has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, but carries an N-fluoro amide and an N-amino indole. Seed 1 instead reaches an amidino/hydrazino-substituted benzene fused to an unsaturated four-membered ring. The Parent leaders retain similarly compact indole carboxamide chemistry; the Child has not opened a wholly different medicinal-chemistry class.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 286 of 870 optimizer molecules, including 57 of the top 87. N-fluoro amides are chemical reactivity concerns, not evidence of a more useful drug-like analogue.

The highest seed-0 family includes halomethylated nitrogen and N-hydroxylated amides; seed 1 includes a fused four-membered unsaturated ring and haloalkyl ethers. These need chemistry-specific stability and feasibility scrutiny.
missing_features: Coverage of alternative compact heteroaromatic cores retaining the favorable amide/aromatic arrangement is limited; most leading molecules repeat one indole-carboxamide connectivity.

Chemically conventional counterparts of the leading N-fluoro/N-hydroxy/N-amino variants are insufficiently explored to establish whether these unusual bonds are needed. The trajectory does not identify an unseen required target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 and seed-2 leaders reach 0.4387992465191 and 0.42956033293511225, whereas the seed-1 fused-four-membered-ring leader reaches 0.37483330611175764. A 51-heavy-atom heteroaromatic/indole assembly scores 5.631227773275544e-23, and the three-heavy-atom ether COC scores 3.563993999218106e-16. Within this observed set, an intact compact aromatic amide framework is associated with higher scores than either extreme size. The cited seed-0 chlorine/fluorine substitution variants tie exactly at 0.4387992465191, so their halogen identity is not an observed improvement. The final seed-2 proposal remains an N-fluoro-amide analogue at 0.40314990987966176. The top 87 records span only five typed and two generic scaffolds, versus 12 and five for the Parent.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 accepted optimizer records, heavy atoms range from 11 to 120 with median 75; the median perceived ring count is 10. Counts at <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 heavy atoms are respectively 0, 0, 746 and 742. Typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 535/437, versus 347/241 in the published Parent. This is the dominant large-molecule tail. Seed 1 builds very large aryl/heteroaryl-ether assemblies containing cyclic O,N carbonyl groups, alkenes, imines and occasional nitriles. Its best molecule has 77 heavy atoms and seven rings. Seed 0's best is a 95-heavy-atom, 16-ring assembly with several four-membered perceived cycles; seed 2's best has 57 heavy atoms, a nine-membered carbonyl-rich N-heterocycle, a carbodiimide, urea/ester groups and an aldehyde. The top 87 molecules have median 90 heavy atoms, versus 32 for the archived Parent top 87. These are elaborate graph assemblies with difficult apparent synthesis, not uniformly compact scaffold hops.
liabilities: 746 of 870 purchases have >=50 heavy atoms and 742 have >50; the maximum is 120. This creates a substantial size and synthetic-complexity burden.

There are peroxide bonds in 133 molecules and in 28 of the top 87; the cited 114-heavy-atom witness contains an O-O linkage despite a high supplied score. Carbodiimides, long imine/polyene chains and O-Cl groups appear in other high or final records.

93 molecules have a perceived fully aromatic cycle of four or fewer atoms, and seed 0's leader contains small fused cycles. These are geometric plausibility flags; the trajectories supply no conformer or synthesis validation.
missing_features: The Child leaders do not combine their heteroaromatic decoration with the compact architecture seen in the higher-scoring published Parent example; useful motif placement is not cleanly separated from repeated fragment growth.

Specified alkene/imine geometry and chemically simpler connections between the same ring systems are missing from the illustrated high-score families. Their score benefit is untested; no exact unseen target structure is inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A small dimethyl/fluoro benzonitrile scores 0.5048144257703081, and a compact carbonyl-rich fused N-heterocycle scores 0.5164082369349414. The three Child seed leaders score 0.6061497326203209, 0.6170759565962307 and 0.601720530109277. Within these Child histories, repeated aromatic/heteroaromatic carbonyl motifs and added unsaturated decoration accompany the higher scores. The cited peroxide-containing 114-heavy-atom molecule still scores 0.6117707639183376, so these scores visibly tolerate a chemically concerning structure. The published Parent's seed-0 leader is a much more compact 30-heavy-atom fused heteroaromatic at 0.8561477222467935; this shows that bulk is not universally required by the observed score landscape, without establishing a paired Child effect. The final seed-2 molecule remains an elaborate carbodiimide/imine assembly at 0.5982257793697878.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 accepted optimizer records, heavy atoms range from 2 to 110 with median 35; the median perceived ring count is 4. Counts at <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 heavy atoms are respectively 1, 1, 35 and 34. Typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 349/239, versus 327/202 in the published Parent. The leading molecules are recognizably aryl-substituted amines: halophenyl and phenol/catechol groups linked to tertiary amines and aza rings. The three seed leaders have 35, 30 and 31 heavy atoms, with an eight-membered diamine plus cyclobutene in seed 0, an N-aryl azetidine and aminoethyl side chain in seed 1, and a six-membered diaza ring with aminoalkyl substituents in seed 2. liabilities: The highest-scoring molecule combines an aldehyde, a substituted azetidine and an N-bromomethyl group; these make stability and synthesis less straightforward than the aromatic/amine motif alone suggests.
No configuration is specified in any of the 856 stereogenic optimizer molecules. The illustrated highly substituted cyclic amines therefore do not identify a unique stereoisomer.
The seed-1 final O-Cl analogue is a direct example of a high score tolerating a reactive bond; the record should not be read as validation of chemical utility.
missing_features: Defined configurations at the crowded aza-ring and benzylic centres are absent, as are explicitly represented protonation states; the records do not test whether either distinction improves the score.

The high-score aryl/amine motif is not consistently realized through chemically simpler analogues without aldehyde, halomethyl or hypohalite appendages. The score supplies no assurance that these appendages are useful interactions.

Counts at <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 heavy atoms are respectively 0, 0, 19 and 17. Typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 534/345, versus 560/380 in the published Parent. The output is rich in N-methyl cyclic amides and lactams connected to phenyl, pyridyl, pyrrolyl/azole or fused aza-aromatic groups, commonly with ethoxy/propyl substituents. liabilities: 237 optimizer molecules have a perceived ring of at least nine atoms, and two seed leaders have ten-membered rings. Such structures are not inherently impossible, but their accessibility and conformation are not established by SMILES validity.

liabilities: The three seed leaders have respectively six, four and six unassigned tetrahedral centres. Their heavily bridged connectivity and unsaturated junctions raise substantial feasibility questions that cannot be settled from a two-dimensional graph.

N-N links, thiols, small unsaturated rings and occasional cumulated bonds occur alongside the fluorinated cyclic carbonyl groups. These liabilities persist even though some N-halogenated variants have lower scores than the leaders.
The isolated FS purchase near the end is a remaining fragment failure, but two <=6-heavy-atom records out of 870 do not support describing fragment collapse as this task's dominant chemistry.
missing_features: The current leading series does not combine its compact fluorinated N-rich composition with the simpler ring connectivity present among the published Parent leaders. More bridges and rings are not demonstrated to supply the missing score-relevant chemistry.

All illustrated leaders omit configuration at several stereocentres. The output lacks stereochemically defined, geometrically characterized versions; the trajectory does not establish which configuration or unseen motif the objective would reward.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 62-heavy-atom early recombination scores 3.2416258040348776e-69. Smaller fluorinated cage-like leaders score 0.34660903589913167, 0.44681439873308604 and 0.4063803493213533. Thus the shown Child gradient favors compact fluorinated N-rich structures over the oversized early assemblies, without showing that dense bridging itself is beneficial. The cited nearby seed-1 cage scores 0.4315940942518976. The much smaller FS proposal at seed-0 evaluation 295 scores 8.605482821433369e-24, so shrinkage alone also fails in the observed set. The Parent seed leaders score 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813 on less densely bridged examples; these remain descriptive archived chemistry comparisons, not a certified paired effect. The final seed-2 molecule retains a fluorinated fused cyclic-carbonyl core at 0.3559345492935138.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7e9f57600099, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session; all counts are derived from its actual trusted staging trajectories. Of 4,350 purchases, 837 have >=50 heavy atoms and 828 have >50, compared descriptively with 46 and 44 in published Parent n-cf8d309c06de. One covered objective contributes 746 of the >=50 cases, while compact leaders remain visible elsewhere. Only four purchases have <=5 heavy atoms and the same four have <=6, so the dominant size concern here is the upper tail. The frozen comparison is not certified paired; no intervention causation is assigned.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size-controlled structural change is not consistently represented: extensive ring-rich growth substitutes for compact alternatives in part of the output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs to express ring, core and linker changes while retaining overall molecular size and useful neighboring motifs, so structural novelty need not require concatenating additional large fragments. The evidence does not justify a universal size cutoff or claim that larger molecules always score worse.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7e9f57600099, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session; all counts are derived from its actual trusted staging trajectories. The 4,350 accepted structures include 565 with N-halogen bonds, 63 with O-halogen bonds, 175 with O-O bonds and 451 with a graph-detected cumulated double-bond motif. Actual high-score witnesses include an N-fluoro amide, a peroxide-containing 114-heavy-atom assembly, and an aryl cyclic amine carrying O-Cl. These are local structural flags, not computed stability or toxicity results; high supplied scores visibly do not exclude them.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not reliably preserve conventional bond environments when decorating otherwise recognizable chemical motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is chemically typed substitution that retains intact functional groups and can generate stable alternatives to reactive heteroatom-halogen, peroxide or cumulated-bond connections. General bond-environment awareness must remain independent of objective identity; no particular score benefit or new reward is established here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7e9f57600099, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session; all counts are derived from its actual trusted staging trajectories. No accepted optimizer structure carries a formal charge, assigned tetrahedral configuration or specified double-bond geometry. RDKit identifies 6,946 unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,757 molecules, including all members of two task-level top-87 subsets. Ring amines, benzylic amines, substituted cages and polyenes are already present. This establishes missing representation in the realized output, not an inability of the underlying representation to encode it or a proven score sensitivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic and ionizable chemistry is produced without explicit configuration or charge-state representation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to preserve or explicitly vary chemically coherent stereochemical and charge states when its edits create such distinctions. It should not equate a neutral, unspecified graph with evidence for one defined stereoisomer or solution protonation state.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7e9f57600099, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session; all counts are derived from its actual trusted staging trajectories. 131 optimizer molecules contain a perceived fully aromatic cycle of four or fewer atoms, and 560 contain a perceived ring of at least nine atoms. Witnesses include a leading fused-four-membered-ring amidine, a 16-ring aromatic assembly and a nonaromatic six-ring fluorinated cage with four unassigned tetrahedral centres. Ring perception is descriptive; no conformer, strain or synthesis result was supplied, and an unusual ring alone is not proof of impossibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-system novelty is not accompanied by evidence that the resulting fused and bridged structures are geometrically accessible.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation and replacement need a vocabulary for coherent ring sizes, junctions, unsaturation and stereochemistry so that increasing connectivity can yield plausible new cores. This is a missing chemical realization capability, not evidence that ring-rich output should be categorically forbidden.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7e9f57600099, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session; all counts are derived from its actual trusted staging trajectories. There are 2,038 typed and 1,366 generic Murcko scaffolds overall, yet one task-level top-87 set has only five typed and two generic scaffolds and another has 15 and ten. Exact-score halogen or peripheral substitution ties occur in the cited trajectories. Other leading subsets retain substantially more scaffold variety, so collapse is local rather than universal. After excluding <=6-heavy-atom fragments, mean within-batch count Tanimoto remains 0.743529, versus a descriptive 0.715720 in published Parent n-cf8d309c06de. These are correlated trajectory descriptions under an uncertified paired comparison, not a component contribution claim.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad aggregate scaffold counts do not translate consistently into distinct, compact alternatives among the leading analogues.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs access to coherent core, ring-connectivity and linker alternatives that retain useful functional groups, beyond changing peripheral atom identity. Chemistry association alone does not identify which search component causes local concentration or prove that diversity itself should become a reward.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
